| `minSyncTopK` | 50 | MinSync semantic default `topK` |
| `minSyncScopedQueryTopK` | 100 | MinSync fetch cap applied when a scope narrows the query |
| `toolDescriptionInstanceScopes` | 8 | Instance scopes listed in one datasource tool description |
| `prefetch.jikjiTopK` | 10 (30 with a rerank model) | Jikji find candidate count |
| `prefetch.minSyncTopK` | 10 (100 with a rerank model) | MinSync retrieve candidate count |
| `prefetch.datasourceTopK` | 10 (20 with a rerank model) | Hits requested from each selected datasource |
| `prefetch.jikjiPathLimit` | 100 | Max Jikji answer paths rendered into the baseline |
| `prefetch.sectionLimit` | 100 | Max results rendered per baseline section |

```json
    "mergedEvidenceCeiling": 1000,
    "prefetch": { "jikjiTopK": 12, "sectionLimit": 30 }
  }
}
```

per-result excerpt) so the model can see where the hit came from. Bound baseline
size with `prefetch.sectionLimit` / `prefetch.minSyncTopK` /
`prefetch.datasourceTopK` / `prefetch.jikjiPathLimit`, not with a per-result
content truncation.

The `prefetch.*TopK` defaults depend on reranking. Reranking is opt-in and runs
only when `rerank.model` names a model; then the pool is wide (Jikji 30, MinSync
100, each datasource 20) and the reranker picks the best. Without it (the
default) each source contributes its own top 10 to the first answer. An explicit
value always wins.

On by default. A search that keeps only the top N *chunks* lets one long
document whose dozens of passages all match fill every slot while a document
only the keyword leg found falls past the cut. The record cut spreads the top N
across documents instead. Turn it off with `limits.recordCut.enabled: false`.

- MinSync and the merged search ask for `depth` times the requested count (3x,
  never past 300 hits), then keep the requested count spread across documents:
  the best half with at most `max(perRecordFloor, topK / perRecordDivisor)`
  chunks per document (8 at `topK` 50), then the best chunk of each document not
  shown yet (`newRecordShare`, default 0.5 of `topK`), then rank order.
- A chunk a search tool already showed during the same run is listed by id
  without its text (`already shown earlier in this run`). A new run resends it.
- Each search tool result is held to `resultChars` (60000). The budget is split
  max-min fairly across the chunks, so one huge chunk is cut with a note instead
  of starving the rest; chunks whose share would fall under `minReadChars`
  (2000) are listed as `not read` with their ids.

|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | true | Set `false` to turn the record cut off |
| `depth` | 3 | Fusion depth, 1-10 |
| `newRecordShare` | 0.5 | Share of `topK` reserved for documents not shown yet, 0-1 |
| `perRecordFloor` | 4 | Fewest chunks one document may keep in the head, 1-300 |
| `perRecordDivisor` | 6 | One document keeps at most `topK / perRecordDivisor` in the head, 1-300 |
| `resultChars` | 60000 | Characters one search tool result may hold |
| `minReadChars` | 2000 | Smallest share worth reading |

```json
{ "limits": { "recordCut": { "enabled": false } } }
```

Measured on the maintainer's own corpus (297 sampled passages, a natural question
and a keyword query each, file-level gold, hybrid mode, top 10): nDCG@10 0.646 →
0.656, MRR@10 0.588 → 0.600, Recall@10 0.825 → 0.830, and the top 10 holds 8.8
distinct files instead of 7.5. The Recall difference is within noise.

and are never settable from model/tool arguments: `maxDocuments`,
`maxItemsPerFeed`, and `maxContentChars` (RSS). `maxContentChars` defaults to

search root became unavailable. Every field is optional; unknown keys fail

| `maxDepth` | 64 | Deepest directory level walked below a root before `walk-truncated` |

so run a refresh after setup and whenever documents change. A never-refreshed
workspace still answers, but without MinSync/Jikji evidence.

Refresh (never a query) auto-installs the binaries: MinSync installs a verified
GitHub release into `<workspace>/.autorag/bin` (`minSync.autoInstall` defaults
to true), and Jikji installs the pinned `jikji-cli` 0.2.1 through cargo (`jikji.autoInstall`
defaults to true; requires the Rust toolchain). A `jikji` older than 0.2.0 on PATH
or in the cache is skipped and replaced by that build on refresh. Set `"autoInstall": false` only
when managing the binary yourself. Refresh is incremental: MinSync syncs only
changed parsed mirrors, and `jikji prepare` reuses unchanged documents. Jikji
roots prepare one at a time (they share one central SQLite file that rejects
concurrent writers). A search root nested inside, or duplicating, another root
is skipped for Jikji because the outer root's index already covers it.

Jikji keeps its prepared corpus (search index, parsed text, wiki, routes) in one
central store, not inside your documents: `<OS data dir>/jikji/index.sqlite`
plus `<OS data dir>/jikji/roots/<id>/` (macOS `~/Library/Application Support`,
Linux `$XDG_DATA_HOME` or `~/.local/share`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%`; override
with the `JIKJI_DATA_DIR` environment variable). The only file `refresh` adds
inside an approved document root is the `.jikji_agent_map.md` guide. Tell the
user that before the first `refresh`, and never delete or edit Jikji's central
store by hand; removing it only forces a full Jikji re-prepare on the next
refresh. Jikji 0.1.x wrote a `<root>/.jikji` directory instead; such a
leftover is now unused and safe for the user to delete. Jikji 0.2.0 and newer
refuse to index a root nested inside, or containing, an already indexed root
(`prepare root overlaps existing indexed root`), which is why overlapping search
roots are collapsed to the outermost one before Jikji runs.

Exact duplicate exclusion is enabled by default. AutoRAG invokes the external
`dupey` CLI before parsed-mirror indexing, keeps the newest filesystem copy for
each exact canonical-text hash, and excludes older copies from the mirror.
Install dupey during setup when it is missing (`command -v dupey || cargo
install dupey --locked`) and tell the user the feature is available; when installation
is impossible, refresh continues without this optimization and the user is
told duplicate exclusion is off. Set `"excludeExactDuplicates": false` to
index every copy.

AutoRAG owns no embedding model. im-not-llm provisions the embedder
(`Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B`, 1024 dimensions) in its own cache
(`~/.cache/im-not-llm/models`); there is no local model download and no bundled
runtime. One shared embedder serves everything that embeds inside
AutoRAG: MinSync indexing/query, memory similar-question search, the
chat-crawler sidecars, the GitHub Gist vector index, and the endpoint external
CLIs are pointed at. The default needs no embedder flags and no API key. It
resolves in order:

1. A configured remote endpoint (`minSync.embedder`), used for everything; no
   daemon is started and no local model is loaded.
2. A running `inl serve` daemon (loopback only).
   AutoRAG never starts it: run `inl serve --idle-timeout 0` yourself, as
   a launchd/systemd service (see `docs/indexing/embedding-backends.md`), or press
   Ctrl+Shift+E in `autorag tui`. `autorag setup` only reports whether it is
   alive.
3. MinSync's in-process engine, through the optional Node-API addon
   `@nomadamas/minsync-native` (same engine and weights, so bit-for-bit
   identical vectors; not bundled). Without a daemon and without the addon,
   embedding fails with an error naming the missing package.

Override the embedder only when intentionally using a remote provider:

```bash
autorag init \
  --embedder-id "voyageai/voyage-4-lite" \
  --embedder-base-url "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1" \
  --embedder-api-key-env "OPENROUTER_API_KEY" \
  --embedder-dimension 1024 \
  --embedder-batch-size 64
```

A remote `minSync.embedder` names an `id` (`openai:<model>`, `tei:<model>`, or
any id together with a `baseUrl`) plus optional `apiKeyEnv` (the **name** of the
environment variable holding the bearer token), `dimension`, `batchSize`, and
`timeoutMs`. OpenAI-protocol endpoints POST `{baseUrl}/v1/embeddings`; a `tei:`
endpoint POSTs `{baseUrl}/embed`; `openai:` with no `baseUrl` means
`https://api.openai.com`. Only store the environment-variable name, never its
value. `dimension` and `batchSize` must be positive integers, and `dimension`
must match the endpoint (the local default is 1024).

### Jev decision model (required) and question decomposition (on by default)

Jev is required: AutoRAG cannot answer without it. Decomposition is on by
default; leave it enabled. Together they make simple questions fast and
multi-part questions thorough.

- **Jev** (`jev`, default `{ "backend": "dazzi" }` when signed in to Dazzi
  Models, else `{ "backend": "openrouter" }`; model `jev-1.13` on Dazzi,
  `typesafe/jev-1.13` on OpenRouter) runs before the fast answer. It routes each question to
  local search (everything needing more information),
  `organize` (moving, renaming, converting, or
  sorting files and folders), `extra` (a knowledge answer, or any other action that needs no
  retrieval, such as committing code: one turn with every tool), or the `config`
  branch, and decides
  whether to decompose it. A non-local branch only wins above a 0.75 confidence
  floor; anything weaker stays on local search. On
  local search it also decides, per registered datasource, whether to search
  it before the fast answer, using each datasource's `description` and where
  similar past questions were answered (retrieval memory). When setting up a
  datasource, always write a `description` from what it actually holds:
  channels or rooms, people, topics, time range (for example `"Team Slack,
  2024-2026: #release and #on-call channels, dependabot notifications"`).
  Jev is told descriptions are short, non-exhaustive summaries, so list the
  main content and do not try to list everything. After the fast answer it
  decides whether verification is needed, so a complete, evidence-backed fast
  answer ends the run.
- **Question decomposition** (`queryDecomposition`, default model
  `dazzi/openai/gpt-6-luna` when signed in to Dazzi Models, else
  `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.7-flash`) splits a multi-part question into at most
  five search queries that run in parallel.

Both need a credential for the chosen backend: a Dazzi Models `/login` (check with
`autorag models list --provider dazzi --available`), or the user's
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (`test -n "$OPENROUTER_API_KEY"`, never print it). The first
question of every session checks that Jev answers; without a working credential
the search stops with `[decision-model-unavailable]` (`autorag search` exits 3,
and `--json` carries `code`, `reason`, `backend`, `model`). Read `reason`:
`missing-credential` means set the key or sign in, `unauthorized` means replace
the key, `model-not-found` means fix `jev.model`, `payment-required` means the
backend account is out of credit, `unreachable` and `rate-limited` mean retry.

```json
{
  "jev": { "backend": "openrouter" },
  "queryDecomposition": { "model": { "provider": "openrouter", "id": "qwen/qwen3.7-flash" } }
}
```

`autorag init` writes these defaults into new configs. To change them:

- Jev backend and model: any provider with decision models, e.g.
  `{ "backend": "openai", "model": "gpt-6-luna" }` (`OPENAI_API_KEY`),
  `{ "backend": "openrouter", "model": "openai/gpt-6-luna-decisions" }`,
  `"typesafe"` (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`), `"vercel-ai-gateway"` (`AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`),
  `"cloudflare-workers-ai"`, or `"opencode"`. List the choices with
  `autorag models list --decision --available`; never invent a model id.
- sLLM fallback: when Jev is unavailable, the session runs on a small chat model
  (default: the decomposition model) and warns `decision-model-fallback`. Set the
  model with `"jev": { "sllm": { "model": { "provider": …, "id": … } } }`, or
  `"fallback": false` to fail instead.
- sLLM as the decision model: `"jev": { "backend": "sllm" }` decides with the
  small chat model alone and never calls Jev (no Jev credential needed).
- Decomposition model: any catalog `provider`/`id`, with the same fields as
  the top-level `model`.
- `"queryDecomposition": false` decomposes with the search model itself.
- Jev cannot be turned off: `"jev": false` and `jev.enabled` are config errors.
  When questions must never leave the machine, AutoRAG is not usable; say so
  instead of editing the config (Jev sends the question text to its backend).

When a user asks the running agent itself to change its settings (switch the
default model, add a provider, check that a provider works), Jev's `config`
branch loads this whole skill into that turn. The agent edits only the active
config file (and `models.json` for a custom provider), verifies with
`autorag health --json` and `autorag models list --available`, and reports each
change as old → new in its final message. It never prints a
credential value and never uses `init --force`.

### Retrieval and ingest caps

`limits` bounds retrieval, baseline prefetch, and the candidate lists handed to
the model. Every field is optional — an omitted field keeps the shipped default,
so add the section only to tighten or widen a specific cap. Values must be
positive integers; unknown keys (and unknown `prefetch` keys) fail config
resolution.

| Field | Default | Controls |
|---|---|---|
| `mergedEvidenceCeiling` | 500 | `search_all_documents` / model-free merge ceiling when the model omits `topK` |
| `singleDatasourceTopK` | 20 | `search_datasource_*` merge default when the model omits `topK` |
| `minSyncTopK` | 50 | MinSync semantic default `topK` |
| `minSyncScopedQueryTopK` | 100 | MinSync fetch cap applied when a scope narrows the query |
| `toolDescriptionInstanceScopes` | 8 | Instance scopes listed in one datasource tool description |
| `prefetch.jikjiTopK` | 10 (30 with a rerank model) | Jikji find candidate count |
| `prefetch.minSyncTopK` | 10 (100 with a rerank model) | MinSync retrieve candidate count |
| `prefetch.datasourceTopK` | 10 (20 with a rerank model) | Hits requested from each selected datasource |
| `prefetch.jikjiPathLimit` | 100 | Max Jikji answer paths rendered into the baseline |
| `prefetch.sectionLimit` | 100 | Max results rendered per baseline section |

```json
{
  "limits": {
    "mergedEvidenceCeiling": 1000,
    "prefetch": { "jikjiTopK": 12, "sectionLimit": 30 }
  }
}
```

The baseline renders each prefetched result's full chunk content (not a
per-result excerpt) so the model can see where the hit came from. Bound baseline
size with `prefetch.sectionLimit` / `prefetch.minSyncTopK` /
`prefetch.datasourceTopK` / `prefetch.jikjiPathLimit`, not with a per-result
content truncation.

The `prefetch.*TopK` defaults depend on reranking. Reranking is opt-in and runs
only when `rerank.model` names a model; then the pool is wide (Jikji 30, MinSync
100, each datasource 20) and the reranker picks the best. Without it (the
default) each source contributes its own top 10 to the first answer. An explicit
value always wins.

### Record cut (`limits.recordCut`)

On by default. A search that keeps only the top N *chunks* lets one long
document whose dozens of passages all match fill every slot while a document
only the keyword leg found falls past the cut. The record cut spreads the top N
across documents instead. Turn it off with `limits.recordCut.enabled: false`.
When on:

- MinSync and the merged search ask for `depth` times the requested count (3x,
  never past 300 hits), then keep the requested count spread across documents:
  the best half with at most `max(perRecordFloor, topK / perRecordDivisor)`
  chunks per document (8 at `topK` 50), then the best chunk of each document not
  shown yet (`newRecordShare`, default 0.5 of `topK`), then rank order.
- A chunk a search tool already showed during the same run is listed by id
  without its text (`already shown earlier in this run`). A new run resends it.
- Each search tool result is held to `resultChars` (60000). The budget is split
  max-min fairly across the chunks, so one huge chunk is cut with a note instead
  of starving the rest; chunks whose share would fall under `minReadChars`
  (2000) are listed as `not read` with their ids.

| Field | Default | Controls |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | true | Set `false` to turn the record cut off |
| `depth` | 3 | Fusion depth, 1-10 |
| `newRecordShare` | 0.5 | Share of `topK` reserved for documents not shown yet, 0-1 |
| `perRecordFloor` | 4 | Fewest chunks one document may keep in the head, 1-300 |
| `perRecordDivisor` | 6 | One document keeps at most `topK / perRecordDivisor` in the head, 1-300 |
| `resultChars` | 60000 | Characters one search tool result may hold |
| `minReadChars` | 2000 | Smallest share worth reading |

```json
{ "limits": { "recordCut": { "enabled": false } } }
```

Measured on the maintainer's own corpus (297 sampled passages, a natural question
and a keyword query each, file-level gold, hybrid mode, top 10): nDCG@10 0.646 →
0.656, MRR@10 0.588 → 0.600, Recall@10 0.825 → 0.830, and the top 10 holds 8.8
distinct files instead of 7.5. The Recall difference is within noise.

Ingest caps are trusted connector options under `datasources.<name>.connector`
and are never settable from model/tool arguments: `maxDocuments`,
`maxItemsPerFeed`, and `maxContentChars` (RSS). `maxContentChars` defaults to
20000 for RSS.

### Refresh safety limits

`refresh` guards the parsed-mirror refresh against deleting a corpus because a
search root became unavailable. Every field is optional; unknown keys fail
config resolution.

| Field | Default | Controls |
|---|---|---|
| `maxDeleteRatio` | 0.3 | Largest share (0–1) of indexed documents one refresh may delete; a bigger deletion above 100 documents is suppressed (`mass-delete-suppressed`) unless the refresh is forced |
| `maxScannedEntries` | 2000000 | Directory entries examined per search root before `walk-truncated` |
| `maxDepth` | 64 | Deepest directory level walked below a root before `walk-truncated` |

A root that is missing, unlistable, or empty while it previously held documents
keeps its mirrors and reports `search-root-unavailable`; see
`docs/indexing/embedding-backends.md`.

## Probe and configure datasource skills (setup wizard)

Use `autorag setup` to probe the embedding backend, MinSync, and known
datasources automatically:

```bash
autorag setup --format json
```

A datasource setup UI is not shipped in this build — do not recommend it for datasource
setup. Configure datasources directly in trusted config, wizard-style:

1. Probe every datasource for setup feasibility before asking the user
   anything: the backing CLI exists (`lazykatok`, `discrawl`, `slacrawl`,
   `wacrawl`, `telecrawl`, `notcrawl`, `mailcrawl`, `wombat`, `lark-cli`) and its
   local store or archive is present. CLI-backed datasources own their own
   archive, index, and authentication, so environment credentials (such as bot
   tokens) are never required or checked for them. Non-CLI connectors
   (such as `github`) require their credential environment variable
   (`GITHUB_TOKEN`).
2. Auto-configure every datasource that probes feasible — write its trusted
   `datasources` entries without asking. For example,
   when Slack (`slacrawl`) and Discord (`discrawl`) are installed with local
   stores present, set both up automatically. Discord uses discrawl's local
   desktop wiretap archive; no Discord bot token is configured or needed.
3. Skip every datasource that probes infeasible (for example Notion or
   Telegram when their CLIs or native stores are not present) and always
   report the skipped list to the user, with what is missing for each.
4. Set up a skipped datasource only when the user explicitly asks for it:
   install or authenticate the backing CLI first, then configure it.
5. E-mail (`mailcrawl`) matters to most
   users — always probe it and report its status, even when it ends up
   skipped.

Datasource skills belong in trusted config. Builtin
template names are `kakao`, `whatsapp`, `telegram`, `slack`, `discord`,
`clawgallery`, `notion`, `github`, `github-gist`,
`mailcrawl`, `obsidian`, `rss`, `lark`, `hister`, and `wombat`. Config keys may be connection
aliases with `"type": "<template>"`. Unknown names are skipped with an
`unknown-datasource-skill` warning; they do not fail config resolution.
`scope` narrows a query to a sub-path as ordinary filtering. Tags are descriptive metadata only, not search filters. MCP `datasourceIds` selects configured connections before retrieval; discover their IDs with `autorag.datasources.list`.

```jsonc
{
  "datasources": {
    "github": { "connector": { "repos": ["owner/repo"], "tokenEnv": "GITHUB_TOKEN" } },
    "github-gist": { "connector": { "tokenEnv": "GITHUB_TOKEN" } },
    "mailcrawl": { "instanceId": "personal", "connector": { "account": "personal", "mailbox": "INBOX", "binaryPath": "mailcrawl" } },
    "wombat": { "connector": { "binaryPath": "wombat", "agents": ["codex", "claude-code"] } },
    "obsidian": { "connector": { "vaultPath": "/path/to/vault" } },
    "rss": { "connector": { "feeds": [{ "url": "https://example.com/feed.xml" }] } }
  }
}
```

# AutoRAG Librarian Skill

Use this skill when AutoRAG is already configured and the user asks to search,
summarize, compare, or answer questions from local PDFs, wikis, notes, research
papers, knowledge bases, or configured datasources.

AutoRAG is the specialized librarian agent. One configured model plans the
search, calls MinSync, Jikji, datasource, and filesystem tools, reads
sources, judges evidence, and curates the final answer. There is no subagent or
separate model role.

Indexing and refresh read source documents and write only under the configured
workspace `.autorag/` directory and Jikji's central store (`<OS data dir>/jikji/`,
plus a `.jikji_agent_map.md` guide in each indexed root). The librarian may
organize, create, or modify the user's own files in local sessions when the
user asks; it never deletes permanently (OS trash only) and lists every change
as old path → new path. Do not move, rename, edit, or delete source files on your own
initiative while searching or diagnosing.

## Preflight

Confirm a config exists at `--config`, `AUTORAG_CONFIG`,
`$AUTORAG_HOME/config.json`, or `~/.autorag/config.json`. Inspect only
non-secret `searchPaths` and `model` metadata, then run:

```bash
autorag duplicates --json
autorag status --json
autorag health --json
```

### Duplicate-file review

Use `autorag duplicates` when the user asks to find duplicate files, choose
likely latest copies, or reduce corpus/index space. The command and the
`scan_duplicate_documents` Agent tool are read-only and never delete or move
source files. Exact means dupey's canonical extracted-text hash matches;
near/contains families require human review. Exact duplicate exclusion during
refresh is enabled by default and can be disabled with
`"excludeExactDuplicates": false` in `config.json`.

### Converting files

The `convert_files` and `list_file_conversions` Agent tools run the
[Filee](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee) command line to convert local
files offline: documents, spreadsheets, slides, HWP/HWPX, images, e-books,
archives, audio, video, data, and subtitles. They work on any path the user
names, not only the configured roots. This is the one exception to the
"never write source files" rule above: a conversion writes a new file and
never touches its source. An existing output name gets a number added unless
the user asks to replace it, in which case pass `overwrite: true`. Never
delete the source unless the user asked.

Each converted file is checked with `dupey compare` against its source, using
dupey's own thresholds, so the report says whether a later scan will group
them: `exact` (same canonical text, for example DOCX to HWPX), `near` (same
document in another format, for example Markdown to TXT), `different` (text
differs, typically layout formats such as PDF), `unsupported` (dupey cannot
read the format, for example HTML or images), or `unavailable` (dupey not
installed). The command line is `filee.binaryPath` if set, else a `filee`/`filee-cli`
on `PATH`, else the pinned [filee-cli](https://github.com/NomaDamas/filee-cli)
release that `autorag setup` (or the first conversion) downloads into
`<AUTORAG_HOME>/tools/filee-cli/`; `"filee": { "autoInstall": false }` forbids that
download. The system prompt carries the conversion map (which format family
converts to which, and the two-step chain when no direct route exists), so plan
from it instead of probing. `"filee": { "enabled": false }` in `config.json` removes both
tools; `filee.timeoutMs` (default 30 minutes) and `filee.dataDir` (Filee's
own settings and engines, `FILEE_DATA_DIR`) tune them.

### Calculating numbers and dates

The `calculator` Agent tool does every calculation the model would otherwise
do in its head; the system prompt and each phase prompt (the fast answer
included) tell the model never to compute these itself. It is read-only,
in-process, and needs no configuration. Operations:

- `evaluate`: exact decimal arithmetic to 40 significant digits (`0.1 + 0.2`
  is `0.3`), `+ - * / % ^ !`, percent and percent change, rounding, sums,
  means, medians, standard deviations, roots, logs, and trig. `exact: false`
  in the result means a step rounded; `exp`, `ln`, `log`, trig, and fractional
  powers are accurate to about 15 digits, not 40. A bare `log(x)` is refused as
  ambiguous; use `ln`, `log10`, or `log(x, base)`.
- `date_diff`, `date_add`, `date_info`: day counts, calendar spans
  (`10 months, 7 days`), month-end clamping (Jan 31 + 1 month is Feb 28),
  weekday, ISO week, and leap year. Dates read as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY/MM/DD`,
  `YYYYMMDD`, `YYYY년 M월 D일`, ISO datetimes with an offset, epoch seconds,
  `today`, or `now`.
- `business_days_between` and `add_business_days`: Monday to Friday minus a
  `holidays` list. The tool knows no public holidays; pass them in.
- `now` and `convert_timezone`: the current time and DST-aware zone
  conversion. An omitted `timeZone` means the host zone and the result says so;
  a datetime with no offset needs its zone. A zone abbreviation other than
  UTC, KST, and JST is refused, and the error names what to pass instead: PST,
  PDT, MST, MDT, EST, and EDT are fixed offsets (PST is `-08:00` all year, so
  it differs from `America/Los_Angeles` in summer), and CST, IST, and BST mean
  several zones, so the user has to say which.

### Excluding local files from the index

`"excludePaths"` in `config.json` lists files or folders (absolute, or relative
to `workspacePath`) that refresh keeps out of the parsed mirror and MinSync.
A folder entry excludes everything under it. Removing an entry and running
`autorag refresh --method minsync` indexes the file again. Excluded sources are
recorded as `user-excluded` skips, so they are not reported as stale. Jikji
indexes the source folders directly and is not refreshed here, so AutoRAG also
drops excluded paths from the `jikji_find` answer pack and from the files Jikji
hands to the verification step as starting points, at retrieval time; the
on-disk `.jikji_agent_map.md` stays complete, and direct
file reads remain available.

`status` is model-free and path-opaque. `health` resolves the single model,
checks credential presence, and normally probes one live completion. If the
model, authentication, configuration, or indexes are unhealthy, use
`autorag-setup` rather than guessing private provider details.

MinSync and Jikji should normally be healthy. Answering a question never
builds or installs them: `autorag refresh` auto-installs both by default and
builds their indexes incrementally. If they are missing or stale, run a full
`autorag refresh` or return to setup rather than silently degrading to
lexical-only search.

## Search

Prefer `--json --debug` when another agent will consume the result.
`--json` alone omits `sessionId`. `--debug` adds session/diagnostics fields and
does not print filesystem paths.

```bash
autorag search "what were the key findings in the Q3 report" --top-k 5 --json --debug
```

`--json --debug` includes `answer`, numbered `results` (`number`, `title`,
`summary`, optional `source`), and `sessionId`. `--json` without `--debug` is
only `answer` plus `results`. Every
bracketed `[n]` citation in `answer` resolves to a `results[].number` of the
same response; an unmatched citation is removed and reported as a
`citation-without-result` diagnostic. Within one conversation (an interactive
session, including a resumed one), a source keeps the `number` it was first
shown with and a new source gets the next unused number, so `results[].number`
can skip numbers and need not start at 1 on a later turn.

To inspect the exact persisted evidence behind numbered results, use:

```bash
autorag evidence <sessionId> --result 1 --json
```

The response includes the original source, retrieval method, stable evidence
ID, raw excerpt/content, and any available `chunkIndex`, `lineNumber` and
`lineEnd` (the chunk's line range in the parsed document), `pageStart` and
`pageEnd` (its 1-based page range, only for PDF, HWP/HWPX and PPTX with real
page boundaries), `section` (the article or heading it sits in), `retrievalResultId`, and metadata. Omit `--result` to inspect every result in
the session. Prefer this command whenever the caller wants detailed chunk text
rather than only the curated summary.

- `--scope` narrows datasource retrieval to a requested sub-path (ordinary
  per-query filtering).
- `--json` is required for programmatic consumption.
- Each search result carries `locations` (`lineStart`, `lineEnd`, `pageStart`, `pageEnd`, `section`)
  when the harness measured where its evidence sits in the parsed document. Quote
  those, not line numbers or counts written in the answer prose; a
  `line-reference-unverified` diagnostic (with `--debug`) flags prose line
  numbers no cited evidence covers, and a `page-reference-unverified` diagnostic
  does the same for pages. Locations are absent for chunks the chunker
  rewrote (such as flattened tables). A page is reported only when the parser
  measured real page boundaries (`pageMode` `layout`) and both ends of the chunk
  land on a placed page: files whose pages are a section-level approximation,
  formats without pages (DOCX, text, spreadsheets), and chunks on a page kordoc
  left empty (a table continued across pages) carry no page. Existing indexes
  gain pages when the next refresh re-parses their paged documents.
- `--debug` is required for `sessionId` and diagnostics in search output.
- `autorag evidence` is the detailed source/chunk inspection path.

Do not bypass the librarian with ad hoc raw search when the user requested
AutoRAG. The search loop can use Jikji, MinSync lexical/vector/hybrid retrieval, datasource retrieval, and

# AutoRAG Librarian Skill

Use this skill when AutoRAG is already configured and the user asks to search,
summarize, compare, or answer questions from local PDFs, wikis, notes, research
papers, knowledge bases, or configured datasources.

AutoRAG is the specialized librarian agent. One configured model plans the
search, calls MinSync, Jikji, datasource, and filesystem tools, reads
sources, judges evidence, and curates the final answer. There is no subagent or
separate model role.

Indexing and refresh read source documents and write only under the configured
workspace `.autorag/` directory and Jikji's central store (`<OS data dir>/jikji/`,
plus a `.jikji_agent_map.md` guide in each indexed root). The librarian may
organize, create, or modify the user's own files in local sessions when the
user asks; it never deletes permanently (OS trash only) and lists every change
as old path → new path. Do not move, rename, edit, or delete source files on your own
initiative while searching or diagnosing.

## Preflight

Confirm a config exists at `--config`, `AUTORAG_CONFIG`,
`$AUTORAG_HOME/config.json`, or `~/.autorag/config.json`. Inspect only
non-secret `searchPaths` and `model` metadata, then run:

```bash
autorag duplicates --json
autorag status --json
autorag health --json
```

### Duplicate-file review

Use `autorag duplicates` when the user asks to find duplicate files, choose
likely latest copies, or reduce corpus/index space. The command and the
`scan_duplicate_documents` Agent tool are read-only and never delete or move
source files. Exact means dupey's canonical extracted-text hash matches;
near/contains families require human review. Exact duplicate exclusion during
refresh is enabled by default and can be disabled with
`"excludeExactDuplicates": false` in `config.json`.

### Converting files

The `convert_files` and `list_file_conversions` Agent tools run the
[Filee](https://github.com/KnifeLemon/Filee) command line to convert local
files offline: documents, spreadsheets, slides, HWP/HWPX, images, e-books,
archives, audio, video, data, and subtitles. They work on any path the user
names, not only the configured roots. This is the one exception to the
"never write source files" rule above: a conversion writes a new file and
never touches its source. An existing output name gets a number added unless
the user asks to replace it, in which case pass `overwrite: true`. Never
delete the source unless the user asked.

Each converted file is checked with `dupey compare` against its source, using
dupey's own thresholds, so the report says whether a later scan will group
them: `exact` (same canonical text, for example DOCX to HWPX), `near` (same
document in another format, for example Markdown to TXT), `different` (text
differs, typically layout formats such as PDF), `unsupported` (dupey cannot
read the format, for example HTML or images), or `unavailable` (dupey not
installed). The command line is `filee.binaryPath` if set, else a `filee`/`filee-cli`
on `PATH`, else the pinned [filee-cli](https://github.com/NomaDamas/filee-cli)
release that `autorag setup` (or the first conversion) downloads into
`<AUTORAG_HOME>/tools/filee-cli/`; `"filee": { "autoInstall": false }` forbids that
download. The system prompt carries the conversion map (which format family
converts to which, and the two-step chain when no direct route exists), so plan
from it instead of probing. `"filee": { "enabled": false }` in `config.json` removes both
tools; `filee.timeoutMs` (default 30 minutes) and `filee.dataDir` (Filee's
own settings and engines, `FILEE_DATA_DIR`) tune them.

### Calculating numbers and dates

The `calculator` Agent tool does every calculation the model would otherwise
do in its head; the system prompt and each phase prompt (the fast answer
included) tell the model never to compute these itself. It is read-only,
in-process, and needs no configuration. Operations:

- `evaluate`: exact decimal arithmetic to 40 significant digits (`0.1 + 0.2`
  is `0.3`), `+ - * / % ^ !`, percent and percent change, rounding, sums,
  means, medians, standard deviations, roots, logs, and trig. `exact: false`
  in the result means a step rounded; `exp`, `ln`, `log`, trig, and fractional
  powers are accurate to about 15 digits, not 40. A bare `log(x)` is refused as
  ambiguous; use `ln`, `log10`, or `log(x, base)`.
- `date_diff`, `date_add`, `date_info`: day counts, calendar spans
  (`10 months, 7 days`), month-end clamping (Jan 31 + 1 month is Feb 28),
  weekday, ISO week, and leap year. Dates read as `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY/MM/DD`,
  `YYYYMMDD`, `YYYY년 M월 D일`, ISO datetimes with an offset, epoch seconds,
  `today`, or `now`.
- `business_days_between` and `add_business_days`: Monday to Friday minus a
  `holidays` list. The tool knows no public holidays; pass them in.
- `now` and `convert_timezone`: the current time and DST-aware zone
  conversion. An omitted `timeZone` means the host zone and the result says so;
  a datetime with no offset needs its zone. A zone abbreviation other than
  UTC, KST, and JST is refused, and the error names what to pass instead: PST,
  PDT, MST, MDT, EST, and EDT are fixed offsets (PST is `-08:00` all year, so
  it differs from `America/Los_Angeles` in summer), and CST, IST, and BST mean
  several zones, so the user has to say which.

to `workspacePath`) that refresh keeps out of the parsed mirror and MinSync.

`autorag refresh --method minsync` indexes the file again. Excluded sources are

lexical-only search.
